      <title>US judge orders Trump to sit for deposition in $10bn lawsuit against BBC</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/22/trump-bbc-lawsuit-deposition-discovery</link>
      <description><p>Judge threatens to dismiss Trump’s BBC lawsuit unless he cooperates with discovery process and sits for deposition</p><p>Donald Trump has been ordered by a US judge to cooperate with the discovery process mandated for his lawsuit against the BBC and to sit for a deposition by 11 December – or else he could be subject to sanctions, including the possible dismissal of the $10bn lawsuit.</p><p>The lawsuit stems from a Panorama documentary aired by the BBC that spliced together two comments made nearly an hour apart by Trump during a rally on 6 January 2021, before the US Capitol riot. The BBC has acknowledged that this specific edit was misleading, but Trump has gone on to claim, falsely, that the BBC did not just edit his speech but used AI to insert words into his speech.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/22/trump-bbc-lawsuit-deposition-discovery">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Marine life in Gulf of Mexico has still not fully recovered from 2010 BP oil spill</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/22/deepwater-horizon-oil-spill-gulf-marine-life</link>
      <description><p>New study reveals dramatic population drops in fish, cephalopods and more after the Deepwater Horizon spill</p><p>Marine life in the Gulf of Mexico plummeted by about 60% after BP’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/bp-oil-spill">2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill</a> and has still not fully recovered, according to a new <a href="https://www.pnas.org/cgi/doi/10.1073/pnas.2616554123">study</a>.</p><p>The April 2010<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2014/jun/05/bp-deepwater-horizon-spill-report-failures-risks"> explosion of an offshore drilling </a>unit 50 miles off the Louisiana coast triggered the largest marine oil spill in history, releasing 134m gallons of oil into the ocean. According to the study published Monday in PNAS, the disaster – which also killed 11 people and injured 17 others – led to the “sudden, severe and persistent declines in the abundance” of marine life for more than a decade.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/22/deepwater-horizon-oil-spill-gulf-marine-life">Continue reading...</a></description>
